sentences.zh: 盧彥倫

translations.literal: Lu Yanlun
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanlun

sentences.zh: 盧彥倫，臨潢人。

translations.literal: Lu Yanlun was a man of Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanlun was a native of Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 遼天慶初，蕭貞一留守上京，置為吏，以材幹稱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Liao Tianqing era, Xiao Zhenyi was defending the Superior Capital and appointed him as a clerk; he was known for his talent and capability.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianqing reign of the Liao, when Xiao Zhenyi was defending the Superior Capital, he took Yanlun on as a clerk, and Yanlun won a reputation for ability and resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 是時，臨潢之境多盜，而城中兵無統屬者，府以彥倫為材，薦之於朝，即授殿直、勾當兵馬公事。

translations.literal: At that time there were many bandits in the Linhuang region, yet the troops in the city had no commander over them; the prefectural office regarded Yanlun as capable, recommended him to the court, and he was at once appointed Palace Attendant and put in charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife around Linhuang at the time, while the garrison in the city lacked a unified command. The prefectural authorities, judging Yanlun capable, recommended him to court, and he was promptly made a palace attendant and assigned to manage military affairs.

sentences.zh: 遼兵敗於出河店，還至臨潢，散居民家，令給養之，而軍士縱恣侵擾，無所不至，百姓殊厭苦之。

translations.literal: The Liao army was defeated at Chuhedian, returned to Linhuang, and was dispersed among civilian households with orders that the people provide for them; the soldiers ran wild in their harassment, reaching everywhere, and the common people were deeply wearied and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liao army was defeated at Chuhedian, it fell back on Linhuang and was quartered among the townspeople, who were ordered to feed the men. The soldiers plundered and bullied without restraint, and the populace suffered bitterly.

sentences.zh: 留守耶律赤狗兒不能禁戢，乃召軍民諭之曰：「契丹、漢人久為一家，今邊方有警，國用不足，致使兵士久溷父老間，有侵擾亦當相容。」

translations.literal: The defending commander Yelü Chigou'er could not restrain them, so he summoned soldiers and civilians and instructed them, saying: "Khitan and Han have long been one family. Now there is alarm on the frontier and the state treasury is insufficient, which has forced the troops to mingle long among the elders; even if there is harassment, you ought to bear with it."
translations.idiomatic: The defending commissioner Yelü Chigou'er could not rein them in. He therefore assembled soldiers and civilians and told them, "Khitan and Han have long been one household. With trouble on the borders and the treasury empty, the army has had to lodge among you for a long time. You must endure whatever harassment occurs."

sentences.zh: 眾皆無敢言者。

translations.literal: No one in the crowd dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: No one in the assembly dared to object.

sentences.zh: 彥倫獨曰：「兵興以來，民間財力困竭，今複使之養土，以國家多故，義固不敢辭。

translations.literal: Yanlun alone said: "Since the armies rose, the people's resources have been exhausted; now they are again made to feed the troops. Because the state has many troubles, on principle one would not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlun alone spoke up: "Since the wars began, the people's means have been drained dry. Now we are asked to support the army again. Given the state's many troubles, we would not refuse in principle.

sentences.zh: 而此輩恣為強暴，人不能堪。

translations.literal: Yet these men indulge in violence as they please, and people cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: But these men commit outrages at will, and no one can endure it.

sentences.zh: 且番、漢之民皆赤子也，奪此與彼，謂何。」

translations.literal: Moreover, both tribal and Han subjects are the emperor's children; to seize from these and give to those—what is that called?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Khitan and Han alike are the emperor's children. To rob one group for another—what sort of justice is that?"

sentences.zh: 初取臨潢，軍中有辛訛特刺者，舊為臨潢驛吏，與彥倫善，使往招諭，彥倫殺之。

translations.literal: When Linhuang was first taken, in the army there was one Xin Woteci, formerly a Linhuang post-station clerk and on good terms with Yanlun, who was sent to summon and persuade him; Yanlun killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin first seized Linhuang, a soldier named Xin Woteci—once a clerk at the Linhuang courier station and friendly with Yanlun—was sent to win him over. Yanlun had him killed.

sentences.zh: 遼授彥倫團練使、勾當留守司公事。

translations.literal: The Liao appointed Yanlun regimental training commissioner and acting commissioner of the defending headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao court appointed Yanlun regimental training commissioner and acting commissioner of the defending headquarters.

sentences.zh: 天輔四年，彥倫從留守撻不野出降。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianfu, Yanlun followed the defending commissioner Tabuye in surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianfu, Yanlun followed the defending commissioner Tabuye in submitting to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 授夏州觀察使，權發遣上京留守事。

translations.literal: He was appointed observation commissioner of Xia Prefecture and provisionally directed the affairs of the Superior Capital defending headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was made observation commissioner of Xia Prefecture and provisionally directed affairs at the Superior Capital defending headquarters.

sentences.zh: 師還，撻不野以城叛，彥倫乃率所部逐撻不野，盡殺城中契丹，遣使來報。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Tabuye rebelled with the city; Yanlun then led his troops in pursuit of Tabuye, killed all the Khitan in the city, and sent envoys to report.
translations.idiomatic: After the army withdrew, Tabuye rebelled and held the city. Yanlun led his men in pursuit, slaughtered every Khitan still in the city, and dispatched messengers to report what he had done.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遼將耶律馬哥以兵取臨潢，彥倫拒守者七月。

translations.literal: Before long the Liao general Yelü Mage took troops to seize Linhuang; Yanlun held out against him for seven months.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Liao general Yelü Mage marched on Linhuang with an army. Yanlun held the city against him for seven months.

sentences.zh: 會援兵至，敵解圍去，因赴闕。

translations.literal: When relief troops arrived, the enemy lifted the siege and departed, and he thereupon went to court.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops arrived, the enemy raised the siege and withdrew, and Yanlun then went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，知新城事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui he was made administrator of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhui he was put in charge of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 城邑初建，彥倫為經畫，民居、公宇皆有法。

translations.literal: As the town was first being built, Yanlun planned it, and both private dwellings and public offices were all laid out according to rule.
translations.idiomatic: When the new town was first laid out, Yanlun planned it so that private homes and public buildings alike followed a coherent design.

sentences.zh: 改靜江軍節度留後，知鹹州煙火事。

translations.literal: He was changed to military commissioner designate of the Jingjiang Army and made overseer of beacon-fire affairs in Xian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner designate of the Jingjiang Army and charged with beacon-fire affairs in Xian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷靜江軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted to full military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，行少府監兼都水使者，充提點京城大內所，改利涉軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan he acted as director of the Palace Storehouse and concurrently commissioner of waterways, served as intendant of the capital inner palace office, and was changed to military commissioner of the Lishe Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianjuan era he served as acting director of the Palace Storehouse and concurrent commissioner of waterways, supervised the capital's inner-palace establishment, and was then made military commissioner of the Lishe Army.

sentences.zh: 未閱月，還，複為提點大內所。

translations.literal: Within less than a month he returned and again became intendant of the inner palace office.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was back at court and again made intendant of the inner palace office.

sentences.zh: 彥倫性機巧，能迎合悼合意，由是頗見寵用。

translations.literal: Yanlun was by nature clever and able to cater to Dao-He's wishes; for this reason he came to be greatly favored and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlun was clever by nature and skilled at winning Empress Dowager Dao's favor, and through this he rose to considerable trust and preferment.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使，為宋國歲元使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to commander-in-chief of the palace guard horse and foot armies and served as Song New Year's envoy.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made commander-in-chief of the palace guard horse and foot armies and sent as the Jin envoy for the Song New Year audience.

sentences.zh: 改禮部尚書，加特進，封郇國公。

translations.literal: He was changed to minister of rites, given the extraordinary promotion rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of rites, granted the extraordinary promotion rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，出為大名尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he went out as prefect of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande he was posted out as prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔彥倫營造燕京宮室，以疾卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered Yanlun to construct the palaces at Yanjing; he died of illness, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was ordered to build the palaces at Yanjing. He died of illness at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子璣。

translations.literal: His son was Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ji.

sentences.zh: 子 璣

translations.literal: Son Ji
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji

sentences.zh: 是時，璣年已七十，詔許朝參得坐於廊下。

translations.literal: At that time Ji was already seventy; an edict permitted him at court audience to be seated in the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: By then Ji was already seventy, and an edict allowed him to take a seat in the corridor when he attended court.

sentences.zh: 複致仕。

translations.literal: He again retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office once more.

sentences.zh: 泰和初，詔璣天壽節預宴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, an edict summoned Ji to the Tian Shou festival banquet.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taihe era he was ordered to attend the emperor's birthday banquet.

sentences.zh: 二年，元妃李氏生皇子，滿三月，章宗以璣老而康強，命以所策杖為洗兒禮物。

translations.literal: In the second year the primary consort Lady Li bore a prince; when three months were complete, Zhangzong, because Ji was old yet hale, ordered that the staff he leaned on be the gift for the washing-of-the-child ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Primary Consort Li gave birth to a prince and the third month was reached, Zhangzong—seeing that Ji was old but still vigorous—commanded that the walking staff Ji used be presented as the gift for the infant-washing rite.

sentences.zh: 章宗幸玉泉山，詔璣與致仕宰相俱會食，許策杖給扶。

translations.literal: Zhangzong visited Jade Spring Mountain and ordered Ji and retired chief ministers to dine together, permitting a staff and attendants to support him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong visited Jade Spring Mountain, he summoned Ji to dine with the retired chief ministers and allowed him a staff and aides to steady him.

sentences.zh: 後預天壽節，上命璣與大臣握槊戲，璣獲勝焉。

translations.literal: Later he attended the Tian Shou festival; the emperor ordered Ji and the great ministers to play polo; Ji won.
translations.idiomatic: On a later birthday celebration the emperor had Ji play polo against the chief ministers, and Ji won.

sentences.zh: 從上秋山，賜名馬。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to the autumn mountain hunt and was granted a famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the autumn hunt in the hills and was given a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「酬卿博直。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This rewards your forthright counsel in the polo match."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This repays your blunt honesty at the polo game."

sentences.zh: 其眷遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the degree of favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Taihe at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 子亨嗣。

translations.literal: His son was Hengsi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hengsi.

sentences.zh: 子 亨嗣

translations.literal: Son Hengsi
translations.idiomatic: His son Hengsi

sentences.zh: 亨嗣字繼祖，以廕補閤門祗候，內供奉。

translations.literal: Hengsi, style Jizu, entered office by hereditary privilege as gate attendant of the privy portal and inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hengsi, courtesy name Jizu, entered service by yin privilege as a privy-gate attendant and inner palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 調同監平涼府醋務，改同監天山鹽場。

translations.literal: He was transferred to associate supervisor of the vinegar monopoly at Pingliang Prefecture, then changed to associate supervisor of the Tianshan salt works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as deputy supervisor of the vinegar monopoly at Pingliang Prefecture, then transferred to deputy supervisor of the Tianshan salt works.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，監萊州酒課，累調監豐州、任丘、汲縣、東平酒務。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he supervised the wine tax at Laizhou and was repeatedly transferred to supervise wine monopolies at Feng Prefecture, Renqiu, Ji County, and Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he left office for mourning. When the mourning period ended he oversaw the wine tax at Laizhou and was successively assigned to wine monopolies at Feng Prefecture, Renqiu, Ji County, and Dongping.

sentences.zh: 課最，遷白登縣令。

translations.literal: His tax collections ranked highest and he was promoted to magistrate of Baideng County.
translations.idiomatic: Because his revenue performance ranked first, he was promoted to magistrate of Baideng County.

sentences.zh: 明昌四年，行六部差規措軍前糧料，入為典給直長，改西京戶籍判官，曆官西京、中都太倉使，中都戶籍判官，尚醖署丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Mingchang he acted under the Six Ministries in arranging army-front grain supplies; he entered service as director of the provisioning office, was changed to household-registration judge of the Western Capital, and successively held the posts of Western Capital and Central Capital granary commissioner, Central Capital household-registration judge, and deputy director of the imperial brewery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Mingchang he served under the Six Ministries arranging grain for the armies in the field. He then entered the capital as director of the provisioning office, became household-registration judge of the Western Capital, and held successive posts as granary commissioner of the Western and Central capitals, household-registration judge of the Central Capital, and deputy director of the imperial brewery.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 大安初，複為典給署丞兼太子家令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he again became deputy director of the provisioning office and concurrently steward of the heir apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Da'an he returned as deputy director of the provisioning office and concurrent steward of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 崇慶元年，遷同知順天軍節度使事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongqing he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Shuntian Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongqing he was made vice military commissioner of the Shuntian Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，兵興，徵調煩急，亨嗣以辦最，遷定遠大將軍，入為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: At that time warfare had begun and levies were urgently pressed; because Hengsi handled them with the best results, he was promoted to General Who Stabilizes the Distance and entered service as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: War had broken out and requisitions were urgent. Because Hengsi handled them with the best results, he was promoted to General Who Stabilizes the Distance and appointed vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，遷莒州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was promoted to prefect of Ju Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he was made prefect of Ju Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，山東宣撫司討楊安兒，亨嗣行六部，兵罷，還州。

translations.literal: In the third year the Shandong pacification commission campaigned against Yang An'er; Hengsi served under the Six Ministries; when the troops were dismissed he returned to his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the Shandong pacification commission campaigned against Yang An'er, Hengsi served under the Six Ministries. When the campaign ended he returned to his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Xingding at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 亨嗣與弟亨益，盡友愛之道。

translations.literal: Hengsi and his younger brother Hengyi fully practiced brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Hengsi and his younger brother Hengyi were models of fraternal devotion.

sentences.zh: 亨嗣初以祖廕得官，大定十六年，父璣為同知宣徽院事，當廕子，亨嗣以讓弟亨益。

translations.literal: Hengsi had first received office through his grandfather's privilege; in the sixteenth year of Dading his father Ji was vice director of the Privy Portal Office and was due a yin privilege for a son; Hengsi yielded it to his younger brother Hengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Hengsi had first entered office through his grandfather's yin privilege. In the sixteenth year of Dading, when his father Ji became vice director of the Privy Portal Office and was entitled to pass office to a son, Hengsi yielded the privilege to his younger brother Hengyi.

sentences.zh: 亨益早卒，子兟。

translations.literal: Hengyi died young; his son was Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Hengyi died young, leaving a son named Shen.

sentences.zh: 兟幼稚，亨嗣盡以舊業田宅奴畜財物與之。

translations.literal: Shen was young; Hengsi gave him all the family's old estates, fields, houses, slaves, livestock, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was still a child, so Hengsi turned over to him the entire family patrimony—fields, houses, slaves, livestock, and goods.

sentences.zh: 毛子廉

translations.literal: Mao Zilian
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zilian

sentences.zh: 毛子廉本名八十，臨潢長泰人，材勇善射。

translations.literal: Mao Zilian's original name was Bashí; he was a man of Changtai in Linhuang, talented, brave, and skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zilian, originally named Bashí, came from Changtai in Linhuang. He was capable and courageous and excelled at archery.

sentences.zh: 遼季群盜起，募勇士，子廉應募。

translations.literal: In the late Liao, bandits rose everywhere; warriors were recruited, and Zilian answered the call.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Liao, when bandits rose across the land, the authorities recruited brave men, and Zilian volunteered.

sentences.zh: 遼主召見，賜甲仗，率百人，會所在官兵捕盜。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler summoned him for an audience, bestowed armor and weapons, and had him lead a hundred men to join the local officials and troops in capturing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor received him in audience, granted him arms and armor, and put him at the head of a hundred men to join local officials and troops in hunting down bandits.

sentences.zh: 以功授東頭供奉官，賜良馬。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed eastern head palace attendant and granted a fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made eastern head palace attendant and given a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 天輔四年，遣謀克辛斡特刺、移刺窟斜招諭臨潢，子廉率戶二千六百來歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianfu the court sent meng'an Xin Ganteci and Yila Kuxie to summon Linhuang; Zilian led twenty-six hundred households in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianfu the Jin sent meng'an Xin Ganteci and Yila Kuxie to win over Linhuang. Zilian brought twenty-six hundred households in submission.

sentences.zh: 今就領其眾，佩銀牌，招未降軍民。

translations.literal: He was now to take command of their multitude, wear a silver plate, and recruit soldiers and civilians who had not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately put in command of these people, given a silver tally, and charged with winning over soldiers and civilians who had not yet surrendered.

sentences.zh: 盧彥倫怒于廉先降，殺子廉妻及二子，使騎兵二千伺取子廉。

translations.literal: Lu Yanlun was angry that Zilian had surrendered first; he killed Zilian's wife and two sons and sent two thousand horsemen to lie in wait and seize Zilian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanlun, furious that Zilian had surrendered first, killed Zilian's wife and two sons and sent two thousand horsemen to ambush and capture him.

sentences.zh: 子廉與窟斜經險阻中，騎兵圍之，兩騎突出直犯子廉。

translations.literal: Zilian and Kuxie were passing through difficult terrain when the horsemen surrounded them; two riders burst out and charged straight at Zilian.
translations.idiomatic: Zilian and Kuxie were making their way through rough country when the horsemen surrounded them. Two riders broke from the ring and charged straight at Zilian.

sentences.zh: 子廉引弓斃其一人，其一人挺槍幾中子廉腋。

translations.literal: Zilian drew his bow and killed one of them; the other thrust with his spear and nearly struck Zilian in the armpit.
translations.idiomatic: Zilian loosed an arrow and dropped one man. The other lunged with his spear and nearly struck Zilian under the arm.

sentences.zh: 子廉避其槍，與搏戰，生擒之，乃彥倫健將孫延壽也。

translations.literal: Zilian dodged the spear, grappled with him, and captured him alive; it was Yanlun's stalwart officer Sun Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Zilian evaded the spear, closed with him, and took him alive. He turned out to be Yanlun's champion fighter Sun Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 餘眾潰去。

translations.literal: The rest of the force scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the party broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 天會三年，除上京副留守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhui he was appointed deputy defending commissioner of the Superior Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhui he was made deputy defending commissioner of the Superior Capital.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼鹽鐵事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was additionally put in charge of salt and iron affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was also given charge of salt and iron monopolies.

sentences.zh: 天眷中，除燕京院都監。

translations.literal: During Tianjuan he was appointed chief intendant of the Yanjing bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjuan era he was made chief intendant of the Yanjing bureau.

sentences.zh: 遼王宗幹問宰相曰：「子廉有功，何為下遷。」；

translations.literal: Prince Zonggan asked the chief ministers, saying: "Zilian has merit—why is he demoted downward?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zonggan asked the chief ministers, "Zilian has rendered service. Why has he been demoted?"

sentences.zh: 宰相以例對。

translations.literal: The chief ministers answered according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers answered that it followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 宗幹曰：「盧彥倫何不除此職？

translations.literal: Zonggan said: "Why does Lu Yanlun not have this office removed?
translations.idiomatic: Zonggan said, "Why not strip that post from Lu Yanlun?

sentences.zh: 子廉之功十倍彥倫，在臨潢十餘年，吏民畏愛如一日，誰能及此。」

translations.literal: Zilian's achievements are ten times Yanlun's; he has been in Linhuang more than ten years, and officials and people fear and love him as on a single day—who can equal this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zilian's achievements outdo Yanlun's tenfold. He has been in Linhuang more than ten years, and officials and commoners respect and cherish him as they did on the first day. Who can match that?"

sentences.zh: 是時盧彥倫已以少府監除節度使，故宗幹引以為比。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Yanlun had already been transferred from director of the Palace Storehouse to military commissioner, so Zonggan cited him for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lu Yanlun had already moved from director of the Palace Storehouse to a military commissionership, which was why Zonggan used him as a comparison.

sentences.zh: 除甯昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of the Ningchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zilian was appointed military commissioner of the Ningchang Army.

sentences.zh: 海陵弑熙宗，子廉聞之，歎曰：「曾不念國王定策之功耶。」

translations.literal: When Prince Hailing murdered Emperor Xizong, Zilian heard of it and sighed, saying: "Does he not remember the prince's merit in settling the succession?"
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hailing murdered Emperor Xizong, Zilian heard the news and sighed, "Has he forgotten the prince's role in putting him on the throne?"

sentences.zh: 乃致仕。

translations.literal: He then retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon retired from office.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 李三錫

translations.literal: Li Sanxi
translations.idiomatic: Li Sanxi

sentences.zh: 李三錫字懷邦，錦州安昌人，以貲得官。

translations.literal: Li Sanxi, style Huaibang, was a man of Anchang in Jin Prefecture and obtained office through purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sanxi, courtesy name Huaibang, was from Anchang in Jin Prefecture and bought his way into office.

sentences.zh: 遼季，盜攻錦州，州人推三錫主兵事，設機應變，城賴以完。

translations.literal: In the late Liao, bandits attacked Jin Prefecture; the people of the prefecture pushed Sanxi to command military affairs; he devised stratagems and adapted to change, and the city relied on this to remain intact.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Liao, when bandits attacked Jin Prefecture, the townspeople put Sanxi in charge of defense. He devised flexible countermeasures, and the city survived intact because of him.

sentences.zh: 錄功授左承制。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was appointed left palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His service was recognized and he was made a left palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 遼主走天德，劉彥宗辟三錫將兵保白雲山。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler fled to Tiande; Liu Yanzong recruited Sanxi to lead troops in defending Baiyun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor fled to Tiande, Liu Yanzong enlisted Sanxi to hold Baiyun Mountain with troops.

sentences.zh: 金兵次來州，三錫以其眾降。

translations.literal: When the Jin army halted at Laizhou, Sanxi surrendered with his forces.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army reached Laizhou, Sanxi surrendered with his men.

sentences.zh: 攝臨海軍節度副使，參預元帥府軍事，改知嚴州。

translations.literal: He acted as vice military commissioner of the Linhai Army, participated in the marshal's headquarters military affairs, and was changed to prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice military commissioner of the Linhai Army and took part in the marshal's headquarters, then was made prefect of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宗望伐宋，三錫領行軍猛安，敗郭藥師軍于白河。

translations.literal: When Zongwang campaigned against Song, Sanxi led a campaign meng'an and defeated Guo Yaoshi's army at the Bai River.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang invaded the Song, Sanxi commanded a campaign meng'an and routed Guo Yaoshi's army at the Bai River.

sentences.zh: 進官安州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was advanced in office to defense commissioner of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to defense commissioner of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 再克汴京，三錫從闍母護宋二主北歸。

translations.literal: When Bianjing was taken again, Sanxi followed Zhamu in escorting the two Song emperors north.
translations.idiomatic: When Bianjing fell a second time, Sanxi accompanied Zhamu in escorting the two captive Song emperors north.

sentences.zh: 複知嚴州，改歸德軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He again became prefect of Yan Prefecture and was changed to vice military commissioner of the Guide Army.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as prefect of Yan Prefecture, then was made vice military commissioner of the Guide Army.

sentences.zh: 詔廢齊國，擇吏三十人與俱行，三錫在選中。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the Qi state; thirty officials were chosen to travel with the mission, and Sanxi was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict abolished the Qi state, thirty officials were chosen to accompany the mission, and Sanxi was one of them.

sentences.zh: 還為慶州刺史，三遷武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as prefect of Qing Prefecture and was promoted three times to military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as prefect of Qing Prefecture and was promoted three times until he became military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.

sentences.zh: 察廉第一，遷三階，改安國軍節度使，除河北西路轉運使，致仕。

translations.literal: In the integrity inspection he ranked first, was advanced three grades, was changed to military commissioner of the Anguo Army, appointed transport commissioner of Hebei West Circuit, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the integrity review, was advanced three grades, made military commissioner of the Anguo Army, appointed transport commissioner of Hebei West Circuit, and then retired.

sentences.zh: 三錫政事強明，所至稱治。

translations.literal: Sanxi's administration was forceful and clear; wherever he went he was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Sanxi was forceful and clear in government affairs, and wherever he served he won praise for good order.

sentences.zh: 世宗舊聞其名，大定初，起為北京路都轉運使。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong had long heard his name; at the beginning of Dading he was recalled to serve as chief transport commissioner of the Beijing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong had heard of him before. At the start of Dading he was recalled as chief transport commissioner of the Beijing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 制下，而三錫已卒。

translations.literal: The appointment was issued, but Sanxi had already died.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment reached him only after Sanxi had already died.

sentences.zh: 孔敬宗

translations.literal: Kong Jingzong
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jingzong

sentences.zh: 孔敬宗字仲先，其先東垣人，石晉末，徙遼陽。

translations.literal: Kong Jingzong, style Zhongxian, was originally from Dongyuan; at the end of the Later Jin he moved to Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jingzong, courtesy name Zhongxian, came from Dongyuan. At the end of the Later Jin his family moved to Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 遼季，敬宗為甯昌劉宏幕官。

translations.literal: In the late Liao, Jingzong was a staff officer under Liu Hong of Ningchang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Liao he served on the staff of Liu Hong of Ningchang.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古兵至境上，敬宗勸劉宏迎降，遂以敬宗為鄉導，拔顯州，以功補順安令。

translations.literal: When Walugu's troops reached the border, Jingzong urged Liu Hong to welcome surrender; Jingzong was then made guide, Xian Prefecture was taken, and for his merit he was appointed acting magistrate of Shun'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Walugu's army reached the border, Jingzong persuaded Liu Hong to submit. He served as guide, helped capture Xian Prefecture, and was appointed acting magistrate of Shun'an for his service.

sentences.zh: 天輔二年，詔敬宗與劉宏率懿州民徙內地，授世襲猛安，知安州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu an edict ordered Jingzong and Liu Hong to lead the people of Yi Prefecture to relocate inland; he was granted a hereditary meng'an and made administrator of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu he and Liu Hong were ordered to relocate the people of Yi Prefecture inland. He received a hereditary meng'an and was put in charge of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 將兵千人從宗望伐宋。

translations.literal: He led a thousand troops in following Zongwang's campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: He led a thousand men in Zongwang's invasion of the Song.

sentences.zh: 汴京平，宗望命敬宗守汴。

translations.literal: When Bianjing was pacified, Zongwang ordered Jingzong to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: After Bianjing fell, Zongwang put Jingzong in charge of the city.

sentences.zh: 嘗自汴馳驛至河北，還至河上，會日暮無舟，敬宗策馬亂流，遂達南岸。

translations.literal: Once he raced by post-horse relay from Bian to Hebei; returning to the riverbank, he found evening had come and there was no boat; Jingzong spurred his horse through the churning current and thus reached the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Once he rode post-horses from Bianjing to Hebei. On his return he reached the river at dusk with no boat available, so he spurred his horse through the turbulent current and reached the south bank.

sentences.zh: 遷靜江軍節度使，曆石、辰、信、磁四州刺史，階光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, successively served as prefect of Shi, Chen, Xin, and Ci prefectures, and was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He became military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, served in turn as prefect of Shi, Chen, Xin, and Ci, and rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 海陵問張浩曰：「卿識孔敬宗否，何階高職下也。」

translations.literal: Prince Hailing asked Zhang Hao, saying: "Do you know Kong Jingzong? Why is his rank high yet his post low?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hailing asked Zhang Hao, "Do you know Kong Jingzong? Why does a man of such rank hold so low a post?"

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「國初，敬宗勸劉宏以懿州效順，其後從軍積勞，有司不知，故一概常調耳。」

translations.literal: Hao answered: "At the founding of the state, Jingzong urged Liu Hong to submit Yi Prefecture in loyalty; afterward he followed the armies and accumulated merit, but the offices did not know, so he received only the usual routine transfer."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao replied, "At the founding of the dynasty Jingzong persuaded Liu Hong to bring Yi Prefecture over. He later campaigned and earned merit, but the personnel offices never took account of it, so he has received only routine postings."

sentences.zh: 明日，除甯昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed military commissioner of the Ningchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jingzong was made military commissioner of the Ningchang Army.

sentences.zh: 徙歸德軍，致仕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Guide Army and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Guide Army and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 李師夔

translations.literal: Li Shikui
translations.idiomatic: Li Shikui

sentences.zh: 李師夔字賢佐，奉聖永興人。

translations.literal: Li Shikui, style Xianzuo, was a man of Yongxing in Fengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shikui, courtesy name Xianzuo, was from Yongxing in Fengsheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，有大志。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited and had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 以廕入仕，為本州監。

translations.literal: He entered office by hereditary privilege and became supervisor of his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service by yin privilege and became supervisor of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，太祖襲遼主於鴛鴦濼，郡守委城遁去，眾無所屬，相與叩門請師夔主郡事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu the Taizu raided the Liao ruler at Yuanyangpo; the prefect abandoned the city and fled; the people had no leader, and together they knocked at the gate asking Shikui to take charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu, when Taizu struck the Liao emperor at Yuanyang Marsh, the prefect abandoned the city and fled. With no one in authority, the people came together and asked Shikui to take charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 師夔許之，乃搜卒治兵。

translations.literal: Shikui agreed and then gathered soldiers and drilled the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shikui agreed, then mustered troops and put the command in order.

sentences.zh: 迪古乃兵至奉聖州，師夔與其故人沈璋密謀出降，曰：「一城之命懸於此舉。」

translations.literal: When Digunai's army reached Fengsheng Prefecture, Shikui secretly plotted with his old friend Shen Zhang to surrender, saying: "The fate of a whole city hangs on this act."
translations.idiomatic: When Digunai's army reached Fengsheng Prefecture, Shikui secretly plotted surrender with his old friend Shen Zhang. He said, "The fate of the whole city hangs on what we do now."

sentences.zh: 璋曰：「君言是矣。

translations.literal: Zhang said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhang said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 如軍民不從，奈何。」

translations.literal: If soldiers and civilians will not follow, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: But what if the soldiers and civilians refuse to go along?"

sentences.zh: 師夔即率親信十數輩詰旦出城，見餘睹，與之約曰：「今已服從，願無以兵入城及俘掠境內。」

translations.literal: Shikui immediately led a dozen or so trusted men out of the city at dawn, met Yudu, and made an agreement with him, saying: "We have now submitted; we hope you will not bring troops into the city or carry off plunder within the district."
translations.idiomatic: Shikui at once led a dozen trusted followers out of the city at dawn, met Yudu, and pledged, "We have submitted. Please do not march troops into the city or plunder the countryside."

sentences.zh: 餘睹許諾。

translations.literal: Yudu promised.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔以師夔領節度，以璋佐之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shikui to head the military commission and made Zhang his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Shikui military commissioner with Zhang as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 賜師夔駿馬二，俾招未附者，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Shikui was granted two fine horses, charged to recruit those not yet attached, and permitted to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He was given two fine horses, told to win over those who had not yet submitted, and authorized to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 明年，加左監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was advanced to great general of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to great general of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 劇賊張勝以萬人逼城，師夔度眾寡不敵，乃偽與之和，日致饋給，勝信之。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Zhang Sheng pressed the city with ten thousand men; Shikui judged that his forces were too few to resist, so he feigned peace with him and daily sent provisions; Sheng trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leader Zhang Sheng pressed the city with ten thousand men. Seeing he was outmatched, Shikui pretended to make peace and sent provisions every day until Sheng trusted him.

sentences.zh: 師夔乘其不備，使人刺勝，殺之。

translations.literal: Shikui seized his unprepared moment, sent men to assassinate Sheng, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng let his guard down, Shikui sent assassins who killed him.

sentences.zh: 以其首徇曰：「汝輩皆良民，脅從至此，今元惡已誅，可棄兵歸複其所。」

translations.literal: He displayed Sheng's head and proclaimed: "You are all good people coerced into following him here; now the chief culprit has been executed; you may cast aside your weapons and return to your homes."
translations.idiomatic: He displayed Sheng's head and announced, "You are all ordinary people forced into this. The ringleader is dead. Lay down your arms and go home."

sentences.zh: 賊眾大驚，皆散去。

translations.literal: The bandit host was greatly alarmed and all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The band scattered in alarm.

sentences.zh: 別賊焦望天、尹智穆率兵數千來寇。

translations.literal: Other bandits Jiao Wangtian and Yin Zhimu led several thousand troops to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Other bandits, Jiao Wangtian and Yin Zhimu, led several thousand men against the city.

sentences.zh: 師夔以兵臨之，設伏歸路，使人反間之。

translations.literal: Shikui advanced troops against them, set an ambush on their line of retreat, and sent men to sow discord between them.
translations.idiomatic: Shikui marched out against them, laid an ambush on their retreat route, and sowed discord between them.

sentences.zh: 智穆果疑，望天先引去。

translations.literal: Zhimu indeed grew suspicious, and Wangtian withdrew first.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhimu grew suspicious as intended, and Jiao Wangtian withdrew first.

sentences.zh: 智穆勢孤，亦還，遇伏而敗，遂執斬之。

translations.literal: Zhimu, isolated in strength, also turned back, met the ambush and was defeated, and was then seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Left isolated, Yin Zhimu turned back as well, walked into the ambush, was defeated, captured, and executed.

sentences.zh: 是後賊眾不敢入境。

translations.literal: After this the bandit hosts did not dare enter the district.
translations.idiomatic: After that the bandits did not dare cross the border again.

sentences.zh: 以勞遷靜江軍節度留後，累遷武平軍節度使，改東京路轉運使，徙陝西東路轉運使。

translations.literal: For his labors he was promoted to military commissioner designate of the Jingjiang Army, was repeatedly advanced to military commissioner of the Wuping Army, was changed to transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital Circuit, and was transferred to transport commissioner of Shaanxi East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made military commissioner designate of the Jingjiang Army, then military commissioner of the Wuping Army, transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital Circuit, and finally transport commissioner of Shaanxi East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 致仕，封任國公。

translations.literal: He retired and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ren.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ren.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 沈璋字之達，奉聖州永興人也。

translations.literal: Shen Zhang, style Zhida, was a man of Yongxing in Fengsheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhang, courtesy name Zhida, was from Yongxing in Fengsheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 學進士業。

translations.literal: He studied for the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He studied for the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 迪古乃軍至上穀，璋與李師夔謀，開門迎降。

translations.literal: When Digunai's army reached Shanggu, Zhang plotted with Li Shikui and opened the gates to welcome surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Digunai's army reached Shanggu, Zhang and Li Shikui opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 明日，擇可為守者，眾皆推璋，璋固稱李師夔，於是授師夔武定軍節度使，以璋副之。

translations.literal: The next day, in choosing one fit to defend the place, all pushed Zhang; Zhang firmly named Li Shikui, and so Shikui was appointed military commissioner of the Wuding Army with Zhang as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when the people chose who should hold the city, everyone nominated Zhang, but Zhang insisted on Li Shikui. Shikui was therefore made military commissioner of the Wuding Army with Zhang as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 授太常少卿，遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was promoted to director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then director of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複山西路都轉運副使，加衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother; when recalled he served as deputy chief transport commissioner of Shanxi West Circuit and was advanced to director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was recalled as deputy chief transport commissioner of Shanxi West Circuit and promoted to director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 從伐宋。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the invasion of the Song.

sentences.zh: 汴京平，眾爭趨貲貨，璋獨無所取，惟載書數千卷而還。

translations.literal: When Bianjing was pacified, the crowd rushed for goods and wealth; Zhang alone took nothing, loading only several thousand scrolls of books on his return.
translations.idiomatic: When Bianjing fell, everyone rushed for loot. Zhang alone took nothing and returned with only several thousand books.

sentences.zh: 太行賊陷潞州，殺其守姚璠，官軍討平之，命璋權知州事。

translations.literal: Bandits of the Taihang range seized Lu Prefecture and killed its defender Yao Fan; government troops suppressed them and ordered Zhang to act as provisional prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Taihang bandits seized Lu Prefecture and killed its defender Yao Fan. After government troops put down the revolt, Zhang was appointed acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 璋至，招複逋逃，賑養困餓，收其橫屍葬之。

translations.literal: When Zhang arrived he summoned back fugitives, relieved and fed the destitute and starving, gathered the corpses lying about and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang arrived he recalled fugitives, fed the destitute, and gathered the unburied dead for proper burial.

sentences.zh: 未幾，民頗軍輯。

translations.literal: Before long the people were largely settled and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the people were largely restored to order.

sentences.zh: 初，賊黨據城，潞之軍卒當緣坐者七百人，帥府牒璋盡誅之，璋不從。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the rebel party held the city, seven hundred soldiers of Lu were liable to collective punishment; the marshal's headquarters sent a dispatch ordering Zhang to execute them all, and Zhang refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels had held the city, seven hundred Lu garrison soldiers were liable to collective punishment. The marshal's headquarters ordered Zhang to execute them all, and he refused.

sentences.zh: 帥府聞之，大怒，召璋呵責，且欲殺璋，左右震恐，璋顏色不動，從容對曰：「招亡撫存，璋之職也。

translations.literal: When the marshal's headquarters heard this it was greatly angered, summoned Zhang to rebuke him, and even wished to kill Zhang; those beside him were shaken with fear, but Zhang's expression did not change, and he calmly replied: "Summoning the lost and comforting the living—this is Zhang's duty.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal's headquarters was furious, summoned Zhang to rebuke him, and even threatened to kill him. Those present were terrified, but Zhang's face did not change. He calmly replied, "Winning back fugitives and caring for the living is my duty.

sentences.zh: 此輩初無叛心，蓋為賊所脅，有不得已者，故招之複來。

translations.literal: These men at first had no heart to rebel; they were coerced by the bandits and had no choice, so I summoned them and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: They never meant to rebel. The bandits forced them, and they had no choice. That is why they came back when I called them.

sentences.zh: 今欲殺之，是殺降也。

translations.literal: If you now wish to kill them, that is killing men who have surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: To kill them now would be to slaughter men who have surrendered.

sentences.zh: 苟利於眾，璋死何憾。」

translations.literal: If it profits the multitude, what regret would Zhang have in dying?"
translations.idiomatic: If my death serves the common good, I have no regret."

sentences.zh: 少頃，怒解。

translations.literal: In a little while the anger subsided.
translations.idiomatic: After a moment his anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 因召潞軍曰：「吾始命戮汝，今汝使君活爾矣。」

translations.literal: He then summoned the Lu troops and said: "At first I ordered you slaughtered; now your prefect has kept you alive."
translations.idiomatic: He then called the Lu garrison together and said, "I first ordered you executed. Your prefect has saved your lives."

sentences.zh: 皆感泣而去。

translations.literal: All wept with gratitude and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They left in tears of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之，拜左諫議大夫，知潞州事。

translations.literal: The court heard and commended him, appointing him left remonstrance councilor and administrator of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of this it praised him and appointed him left remonstrance councilor and prefect of Lu.

sentences.zh: 百姓為之立祠。

translations.literal: The common people erected a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: The people erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 移知忻州，改同知太原尹，加尚書禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Xin Prefecture, was changed to vice prefect of Taiyuan, and was advanced to vice minister of rites in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xin Prefecture, made vice prefect of Taiyuan, and promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時介休人張覺聚黨亡命山谷，鈔掠邑縣，招之不肯降，曰：「前嘗有降者，皆殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jue of Jiexiu gathered a party and fled into the mountain valleys, raiding districts and counties; when summoned he would not surrender, saying: "Before, those who surrendered were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Jue of Jiexiu gathered followers in the hills and raided the counties. He refused to surrender, saying, "Everyone who surrendered before was killed.

sentences.zh: 今以好言誘我，是欲殺我耳。

translations.literal: Now with fine words you lure me—this is because you wish to kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Your kind words now are just another way to get me killed.

sentences.zh: 獨得侍郎沈公一言，我乃無疑。」

translations.literal: Only if I obtain a single word from Vice Minister Shen will I have no doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Only a single promise from Vice Minister Shen would put my mind at ease."

sentences.zh: 於是，命璋往招之，覺即日降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang was ordered to go summon him, and Jue surrendered the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was therefore sent to win him over, and Jue surrendered the same day.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書吏部侍郎、西京副留守、同知平陽尹，遷利涉軍節度使，為東京路都轉運使，改鎮西軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of personnel in the Secretariat, deputy defending commissioner of the Western Capital, and vice prefect of Pingyang; he was promoted to military commissioner of the Lishe Army, served as chief transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital Circuit, and was changed to military commissioner of the Zhenxi Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of personnel, deputy defending commissioner of the Western Capital, and vice prefect of Pingyang, then military commissioner of the Lishe Army, chief transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital Circuit, and finally military commissioner of the Zhenxi Army.

sentences.zh: 天德元年，以病致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiande he retired because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiande he retired due to illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 子宜中，天德三年，賜楊建中榜及第。

translations.literal: His son Yizhong, in the third year of Tiande, was granted passage of the Yang Jianzhong examination list.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yizhong passed the civil service examination in the third year of Tiande on the Yang Jianzhong list.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：危難之際，兩軍方爭，專城之將，國家之輕重系焉。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In moments of peril, when two armies are contending, the general who holds a city alone bears the weight of the state's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: In times of crisis, when two armies are locked in struggle, the commander who holds a city alone carries the state's fortunes on his shoulders.

sentences.zh: 李師夔非有君命，為眾所推，又能全活其人，猶有說也。

translations.literal: Li Shikui had no ruler's command but was pushed forward by the multitude, yet could also preserve the lives of the people—this still admits of explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shikui had no imperial order when the people pressed him to lead, yet he was able to save their lives. That much can still be defended.

sentences.zh: 盧彥倫之降，雖雲城潰，初志不確，何尤乎毛子廉。

translations.literal: Lu Yanlun's surrender, though said to be because the city collapsed, showed an unsteady initial resolve—why blame Mao Zilian?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanlun's surrender, though explained as the collapse of the city, showed an unsteady purpose from the start. Why blame Mao Zilian?

sentences.zh: 至如子廉不仕海陵，沈璋以片言降張覺，一善足稱，何可掩也。

translations.literal: As for Zilian's refusal to serve Prince Hailing, and Shen Zhang's bringing Zhang Jue down with a single phrase—one good deed is enough to win praise; how could these be concealed?
translations.idiomatic: As for Zilian's refusal to serve under Prince Hailing, and Shen Zhang's winning Zhang Jue over with a single promise—one good act is enough to earn praise. Such deeds cannot be hidden.

sentences.zh: 左企弓

translations.literal: Zuo Qigong
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Qigong

sentences.zh: 左企弓字君材。

translations.literal: Zuo Qigong, style Juncai.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Qigong, courtesy name Juncai.

sentences.zh: 八世祖皓，後唐棣川刺史，以行軍司馬戍燕，遼取燕，使守薊，因家焉。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Hao was prefect of Dichuan in the Later Tang; as campaign marshal he garrisoned Yan; when the Liao took Yan they had him guard Ji, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor eight generations back, Hao, was prefect of Dichuan under the Later Tang. Posted to Yan as campaign marshal, he remained when the Liao seized the region and was put in charge of Ji, where the family settled.

sentences.zh: 企弓讀書，通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: Qigong studied books and mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong was a scholar who mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 中進士，再遷來州觀察判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was twice promoted to observation commissioner judge of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose twice to observation commissioner judge of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 蕭英弼賊昭懷太子，窮治黨與，多連引。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yingbi was deemed a traitor against Crown Prince Zhaohuai, party members were exhaustively prosecuted and many were implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yingbi was charged with treason against Crown Prince Zhaohuai, the authorities prosecuted his associates relentlessly and implicated many others.

sentences.zh: 企弓辨析其冤，免其甚眾。

translations.literal: Qigong analyzed and clarified their wrongful accusations and spared a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong exposed the false charges and saved a great many from punishment.

sentences.zh: 自禦史知難事，出為中京副留守，按刑遼陽。

translations.literal: From censor in charge of difficult cases he went out as deputy defending commissioner of the Central Capital and conducted criminal review in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as censor for difficult cases, he became deputy defending commissioner of the Central Capital and conducted criminal review in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 有獄本輕而入之重者，已奏待報，企弓釋之以聞。

translations.literal: There was a case originally light but entered as heavy; it had already been memorialized awaiting reply; Qigong released the prisoner and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In one case a light offense had been entered as a heavy one and memorialized for approval. Qigong released the prisoner and reported what he had done.

sentences.zh: 累遷知三司使事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 天慶末，拜廣陵軍節度使，同中書門下平章事、知樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianqing he was appointed military commissioner of the Guangling Army, given the concurrent titles of co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and director of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianqing era he was made military commissioner of the Guangling Army, co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and director of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 金兵已拔上京，北樞密院恐忤旨，不以時奏。

translations.literal: The Jin army had already taken the Superior Capital, but the Northern Privy Council feared offending the throne and did not report it in time.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had already captured the Superior Capital, but the Northern Privy Council, fearing to displease the throne, failed to report it promptly.

sentences.zh: 遼故事，軍政皆關決北樞密院，然後奏禦。

translations.literal: By Liao precedent, all military and civil affairs were decided through the Northern Privy Council before being memorialized to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liao precedent, military and civil affairs had to pass through the Northern Privy Council before being reported to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 企弓以聞。

translations.literal: Qigong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong reported the news himself.

sentences.zh: 遼主曰：「兵事無乃非卿職邪？」

translations.literal: The Liao ruler said: "Military affairs—are they not outside your duty?"
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor said, "Military affairs are not your responsibility, are they?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「國勢如此，豈敢循例為自容計。」

translations.literal: He answered: "The state's situation is such—how would I dare follow precedent to calculate my own safety?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "With the realm in this condition, how could I cling to precedent for my own safety?"

sentences.zh: 因陳守備之策。

translations.literal: He then set forth plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented plans for defense.

sentences.zh: 拜中書侍郎平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, co-director, and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, co-director, and supervisor of the national history compilation.

sentences.zh: 時遼主聞金已克中京，將西幸以避之。

translations.literal: At that time the Liao ruler heard the Jin had taken the Central Capital and was about to move west on a progress to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor then heard that the Jin had taken the Central Capital and planned to move west to escape them.

sentences.zh: 企弓諫不聽。

translations.literal: Qigong remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong remonstrated, but his advice went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 遼主自鴛鴦濼亡保陰山。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler fled from Yuanyang Marsh to hold out in the Yin Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor fled from Yuanyang Marsh and took refuge in the Yin Mountains.

sentences.zh: 秦晉國王耶律捏裏自立于燕，廢遼主為湘陰王，改元德興。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin and Jin, Yelü Nieli, declared himself in Yan, deposed the Liao ruler as Prince of Xiangyin, and changed the era name to Dexing.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin and Jin, Yelü Nieli, set himself up in Yan, demoted the Liao emperor to Prince of Xiangyin, and proclaimed the Dexing era.

sentences.zh: 企弓守司徒，封燕國公。

translations.literal: Qigong remained minister of education and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong retained the post of minister of education and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 虞仲文參知政事，領西京留守、同中書門下平章事、內外諸軍都統。

translations.literal: Yu Zhongwen was participant in governance, headed the Western Capital defending headquarters, served as co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and was commander-in-chief of all internal and external armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhongwen became participant in governance, defending commissioner of the Western Capital, co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and commander-in-chief of all armies within and without.

sentences.zh: 曹勇義中書侍郎平章事、樞密使、燕國公。

translations.literal: Cao Yongyi was vice director of the Secretariat, co-director, privy councilor, and Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yongyi was vice director of the Secretariat, co-director, privy councilor, and Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 康公弼參知政事、簽樞密院事，賜號「忠烈翊聖功臣」。

translations.literal: Kang Gongbi was participant in governance and signatory of the Privy Council, and was granted the title "Meritorious Minister Who Loyalty and Fierceness Assist the Sage."
translations.idiomatic: Kang Gongbi was participant in governance and signatory of the Privy Council, and was granted the title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Fierceness Assisting the Sage.

sentences.zh: 德妃攝政，企弓加侍中。

translations.literal: The Virtuous Consort acted as regent, and Qigong was advanced to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Virtuous Consort served as regent, and Qigong was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 宋兵襲燕，奄至城中，已而敗走。

translations.literal: Song troops raided Yan, suddenly reaching the city, then were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces raided Yan and burst into the city, but were soon beaten back.

sentences.zh: 或疑有內應者，欲根株之，企弓爭之，乃止。

translations.literal: Some suspected there had been collaborators within and wished to root them out completely; Qigong argued against it, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Some suspected collaborators inside the city and wanted a thorough purge. Qigong objected, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 太祖至居庸關，蕭妃自古北口遁去。

translations.literal: When the Taizu reached Juyong Pass, the Xiao consort fled through the ancient northern route.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu reached Juyong Pass, the Xiao consort fled by the northern road.

sentences.zh: 都監高六等送款于太祖，太祖徑至城下。

translations.literal: Chief intendant Gao Liu and others offered submission to the Taizu, and the Taizu went straight to the foot of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Chief intendant Gao Liu and others surrendered to Taizu, who marched straight to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 高六等開門待之。

translations.literal: Gao Liu and the others opened the gates to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Liu opened the gates to receive him.

sentences.zh: 太祖入城受降，企弓等猶不知。

translations.literal: The Taizu entered the city to accept surrender, while Qigong and the others still did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu entered the city to accept surrender while Qigong and his colleagues were still unaware.

sentences.zh: 太祖駐蹕燕京城南，企弓等奉表降，太祖俾復舊職，皆受金牌。

translations.literal: The Taizu halted south of Yanjing; Qigong and the others presented a memorial of surrender; the Taizu had them resume their former offices, and all received gold plates.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu encamped south of Yanjing. Qigong and the others submitted a memorial of surrender. Taizu restored them to their former offices and granted each a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 企弓守太傅、中書令，仲文樞密使、侍中、秦國公，勇義以舊官守司空，公弼同中書門下平章事、樞密副使權知院事、簽中書省、封陳國公。

translations.literal: Qigong remained grand mentor and director of the Secretariat; Zhongwen was privy councilor, palace attendant, and Duke of Qin; Yongyi kept his former office as minister of works; Gongbi was co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, vice privy councilor with acting charge of the council, signatory of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong remained grand mentor and director of the Secretariat. Zhongwen was privy councilor, palace attendant, and Duke of Qin. Yongyi kept his old post as minister of works. Gongbi was co-director, acting vice privy councilor, Secretariat signatory, and Duke of Chen.

sentences.zh: 遼致仕宰相張琳進上降表，詔曰：「燕京應琳田宅財物並給還之。」

translations.literal: The retired Liao chief minister Zhang Lin presented a surrender memorial; an edict said: "In Yanjing, Lin's fields, houses, and goods are all to be returned to him."
translations.idiomatic: The retired Liao chief minister Zhang Lin submitted a surrender memorial. An edict declared, "Zhang Lin's lands, houses, and goods in Yanjing are all to be returned to him."

sentences.zh: 琳年高，不能入見，止令其子弟來。

translations.literal: Lin was advanced in years and could not come for an audience; he was only ordered to send his sons and younger relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was too old to attend in person and was told only to send his sons and younger kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 太祖既定燕，從初約，以與宋人。

translations.literal: After the Taizu had secured Yan, according to the original agreement he gave it to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu secured Yan, he honored the original agreement and handed it over to the Song.

sentences.zh: 企弓獻詩，略曰：「君王莫聽捐燕議，一寸山河一寸金。」

translations.literal: Qigong presented a poem, which in essence said: "My lord, do not heed counsel to give up Yan—every inch of territory is an inch of gold."
translations.idiomatic: Qigong presented a poem that ran, in essence, "My lord, do not heed counsel to surrender Yan—every inch of land is an inch of gold."

sentences.zh: 太祖不聽。

translations.literal: The Taizu did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu would not be persuaded.

sentences.zh: 是時，置樞密院于廣寧府。

translations.literal: At that time the Privy Council was established at Guangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Privy Council was set up at Guangning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 企弓等將赴廣甯，張覺在平州有異志，太祖欲以兵送之。

translations.literal: Qigong and the others were about to go to Guangning; Zhang Jue at Ping Prefecture harbored a different intent, and the Taizu wished to escort them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong and his colleagues were about to travel to Guangning. Zhang Jue at Ping Prefecture had other designs, and Taizu wanted to send troops as escort.

sentences.zh: 企弓等辭兵曰：「如此，是促之亂也。」

translations.literal: Qigong and the others declined troops, saying: "In this way you would hasten rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: They declined the escort, saying, "That would only provoke rebellion."

sentences.zh: 及過平州，舍于栗林下，張覺使人殺之。

translations.literal: When they passed Ping Prefecture and lodged beneath the chestnut grove, Zhang Jue sent men to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: When they passed through Ping Prefecture and lodged at Chestnut Grove, Zhang Jue had them murdered.

sentences.zh: 企弓年七十三，諡恭烈。

translations.literal: Qigong was seventy-three; his posthumous title was Gonglie.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong was seventy-three. His posthumous title was Gonglie, "Respectful and Fierce."

sentences.zh: 天會七年，贈守太師，遣使致奠。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui he was posthumously granted acting grand mentor and envoys were sent to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianhui he was posthumously made acting grand mentor, and envoys were sent to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，改贈特進、濟國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he was changed to posthumous extraordinary promotion and Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong his posthumous honors were raised to extraordinary promotion and Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 虞仲文

translations.literal: Yu Zhongwen
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhongwen

sentences.zh: 虞仲文字質夫，武州寧遠人也。

translations.literal: Yu Zhongwen, style Zhifu, was a man of Ningyuan in Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhongwen, courtesy name Zhifu, was from Ningyuan in Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七歲知作詩，十歲能屬文，日記千言，刻苦學問。

translations.literal: At seven he knew how to compose poetry; at ten he could write prose; he recorded a thousand words daily and studied with bitter diligence.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could write poetry; at ten he could compose prose. He wrote a thousand characters a day and pursued his studies with relentless discipline.

sentences.zh: 第進士，累仕州縣，以廉能稱。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served repeatedly in prefectures and counties, and was known for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served in successive prefectural and county posts, winning a reputation for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正，對策優等。

translations.literal: He was recommended as worthy and upright, and in the policy examination he ranked in the superior grade.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as worthy and upright, he took top honors in the policy examination.

sentences.zh: 擢起居郎、史館修撰，三遷至太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attendant of the palace secretariat and compiler in the History Office, and was transferred three times until he reached vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant of the palace secretariat and compiler in the History Office, and was promoted three times to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宰相有左降，仲文獨出餞之。

translations.literal: When a chief minister was demoted, Zhongwen alone went out to give him a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: When a chief minister was demoted, Zhongwen alone went out to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 或指以為党，仲文乃求養親。

translations.literal: Some pointed to this as factionalism, so Zhongwen requested leave to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Some accused him of forming a faction, so he asked leave to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 久之，召複前職。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned back to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 宰相薦文行第一，權知制誥，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: The chief ministers recommended him first in literary conduct; he was provisionally put in charge of edicts and appointed secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers ranked him first in literary conduct. He was put in provisional charge of edicts and made a secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 討平白嵆，拜樞密直學士，權翰林學士，為翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: When the Baiqi were suppressed and pacified, he was appointed privy council academician, acting Hanlin academician, and Hanlin exposition academician.
translations.idiomatic: After the Baiqi rebellion was put down, he became privy council academician, acting Hanlin academician, and Hanlin exposition academician.

sentences.zh: 年五十五，卒，諡文正。

translations.literal: At fifty-five he died; his posthumous title was Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-five and was given the posthumous title Wenzheng, "Correct in Culture."

sentences.zh: 天會七年，贈兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui he was posthumously granted concurrent director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianhui he was posthumously made concurrent director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，改贈特進、濮國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he was changed to posthumous extraordinary promotion and Duke of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong his posthumous honors were raised to extraordinary promotion and Duke of Pu.

sentences.zh: 曹勇義

translations.literal: Cao Yongyi
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yongyi

sentences.zh: 曹勇義，廣寧人。

translations.literal: Cao Yongyi was a man of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yongyi was a native of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 第進士，除長春令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Changchun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was made magistrate of Changchun.

sentences.zh: 樞府辟令史。

translations.literal: The Privy Council recruited him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The Privy Council recruited him as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 上書陳時政，累擢館閣，遷樞密副都承旨，權燕京三司使，加給事中。

translations.literal: He memorialized on current policy, was repeatedly promoted in the palace libraries, was transferred to vice chief privy council receptionist, acted as Yanjing director of the Three Departments, and was advanced to supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials on state affairs, rose through the palace libraries, became vice chief privy council receptionist and acting Yanjing director of the Three Departments, and was promoted to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 召為樞密副使，加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice privy councilor and advanced to junior guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice privy councilor and made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 與大公鼎、虞仲文、龔誼友善。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Da Gongding, Yu Zhongwen, and Gong Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Da Gongding, Yu Zhongwen, and Gong Yi.

sentences.zh: 與虞仲文同在樞密，群小擠之。

translations.literal: He and Yu Zhongwen were together in the Privy Council, and petty men crowded them out.
translations.idiomatic: While he and Yu Zhongwen served together in the Privy Council, petty rivals forced them out.

sentences.zh: 複出為三司使，加宣政殿大學士。

translations.literal: He again went out as director of the Three Departments and was advanced to grand academician of the Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as director of the Three Departments and was made grand academician of the Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文莊。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Wenzhuang, "Correct in Letters."

sentences.zh: 天會七年，贈守太保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui he was posthumously granted acting grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianhui he was posthumously made acting grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，改贈特進、定國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he was changed to posthumous extraordinary promotion and Duke of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong his posthumous honors were raised to extraordinary promotion and Duke of Ding.

sentences.zh: 康公弼

translations.literal: Kang Gongbi
translations.idiomatic: Kang Gongbi

sentences.zh: 康公弼字伯迪，其先應州人。

translations.literal: Kang Gongbi, style Bodi, was originally from Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Gongbi, courtesy name Bodi, came from Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖胤，遼保甯間以戰功授質券，家于燕之宛平。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yin, during the Baoning era of the Liao, was granted a pledge certificate for military merit and settled the family in Wanping of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yin received a pledge certificate for military merit during the Liao Baoning era, and the family settled in Wanping in Yan.

sentences.zh: 公弼好學，年二十三中進士，除著作郎、武州軍事判官。

translations.literal: Gongbi loved learning; at twenty-three he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed editing clerk and military judge of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi loved learning. He passed the jinshi examination at twenty-three and was made editing clerk and military judge of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辟樞府令史，求外補，出為寧遠令。

translations.literal: He was recruited as a Privy Council clerk, sought an outside appointment, and went out as magistrate of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited as a Privy Council clerk, he sought a field appointment and was posted as magistrate of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 縣中隕霜殺禾稼，漕司督賦急，系之獄。

translations.literal: In the county, falling frost destroyed the grain crop; the transport office pressed urgently for tax collection and had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Frost destroyed the county's crops. The transport office pressed hard for taxes and had him thrown in prison.

sentences.zh: 公弼上書，朝廷乃釋之，因免縣中租賦，縣人為立生祠。

translations.literal: Gongbi memorialized upward; the court then released him and exempted the county's rents and levies, and the county people erected a living shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi appealed to court. He was released, the county's rents and levies were remitted, and the people erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 監平州錢帛庫，調役糧於川州。

translations.literal: He supervised the money and silk treasury at Ping Prefecture and arranged transport of grain levies at Chuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the money and silk treasury at Ping Prefecture and arranged grain transport at Chuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大盜侯概陷川州，使護送公弼出境，曰：「良吏也。」

translations.literal: The great bandit Hou Kai seized Chuan Prefecture and had Gongbi escorted out of the territory, saying: "A good official."
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chieftain Hou Kai seized Chuan Prefecture but had Gongbi escorted safely out of the region, saying, "He is a good official."

sentences.zh: 權乾州節度使。

translations.literal: He acted as military commissioner of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting military commissioner of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡忠肅。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Zhongsu, "Loyal and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 天會七年，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui he was posthumously granted palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianhui he was posthumously made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，改贈特進、道國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he was changed to posthumous extraordinary promotion and Duke of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong his posthumous honors were raised to extraordinary promotion and Duke of Dao.

sentences.zh: 企弓子泌、瀛、淵。

translations.literal: Qigong's sons were Bi, Ying, and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qigong's sons were Bi, Ying, and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 泌字長源，企弓長子也。

translations.literal: Bi, style Changyuan, was Qigong's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, courtesy name Changyuan, was Qigong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 仕遼，官至棣州刺史。

translations.literal: He served the Liao and reached the office of prefect of Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Liao and rose to prefect of Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖平燕，泌從企弓歸朝。

translations.literal: When the Taizu pacified Yan, Bi followed Qigong in submitting to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified Yan, Bi followed Qigong in submitting to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 既而東遷至平州，企弓為張覺所害，泌複還燕。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they moved east to Ping Prefecture; Qigong was killed by Zhang Jue, and Bi returned again to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: They then moved east to Ping Prefecture. After Qigong was killed by Zhang Jue, Bi returned to Yan.

sentences.zh: 是時，以燕與宋，宣撫司遣至汴，泌以平州仇人在是，乃間道奔還。

translations.literal: At that time Yan was given to the Song; the pacification office sent him to Bian; because enemies from Ping Prefecture were there, he took a bypath and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was then handed to the Song, and the pacification office sent him to Bianjing. Because enemies from Ping Prefecture were there, he slipped away by a back route and returned.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，擢西上閤門使。

translations.literal: The court commended him and promoted him to western upper privy-gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his conduct and promoted him to western upper privy-gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從宋王宗望南伐，破真定有功，知祁州，曆刺澤、隰等州。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Zongwang of Song in the southern campaign, had merit in defeating Zhending, administered Qi Prefecture, and successively served as prefect of Ze, Xi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Zongwang south, helped defeat Zhending, administered Qi Prefecture, and served in turn as prefect of Ze, Xi, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，為浚州防禦使，遷陝西路轉運使，封戴國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was defense commissioner of Jun Prefecture, was transferred to transport commissioner of Shaanxi West Circuit, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Dai.
