translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenyuan he was defense commissioner of Jun Prefecture, then transport commissioner of Shaanxi West Circuit, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Dai.

sentences.zh: 泌性夷澹，好讀《莊》、《老》，年六十一，即請致仕。

translations.literal: Bi was by nature mild and detached, loved reading the Zhuangzi and Laozi, and at sixty-one immediately requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was mild and detached by nature, loved the Zhuangzi and Laozi, and at sixty-one asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 親友或以為早，泌歎曰：「予年三十秉旄鉞，侵尋仕路又三十年，名遂身退，可矣。」

translations.literal: Relatives and friends thought this early; Bi sighed and said: "At thirty I held commander's banners and axes; creeping along the official path for another thirty years—fame achieved and the body withdrawn is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Friends thought this early, but Bi sighed and said, "At thirty I took up command. Another thirty years on the official road is enough. Fame achieved, it is time to withdraw."

sentences.zh: 時人高之。

translations.literal: People of the time held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 弟 淵

translations.literal: Younger brother Yuan
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuan

sentences.zh: 子 光慶

translations.literal: Son Guangqing
translations.idiomatic: His son Guangqing

sentences.zh: 光慶字君錫，幼潁悟，沉厚少言。

translations.literal: Guangqing, style Junxi, was clever in youth, deep and steady, and spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqing, courtesy name Junxi, was clever as a child, grave and steady, and spoke little.

sentences.zh: 淵嘗謂所親曰：「世吾家者，此子也。」

translations.literal: Yuan once told those close to him: "The one who will carry on our house is this boy."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan once told his intimates, "This boy will carry on our family line."

sentences.zh: 以廕，補閤門祗候，遷西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he was appointed privy-gate attendant and was transferred to western upper deputy privy-gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege he became a privy-gate attendant and was promoted to western upper deputy privy-gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複東上閤門副使，再轉西上、東上閤門使，兼太廟署令。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his father; when recalled he served as eastern upper deputy privy-gate commissioner, was again transferred to western and eastern upper privy-gate commissioner, and concurrently director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was recalled as eastern upper deputy privy-gate commissioner, then promoted to western and eastern upper privy-gate commissioner and concurrent director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Office.

sentences.zh: 光慶好古，讀書識大義，喜為詩，善篆隸，尤工大字。

translations.literal: Guangqing loved antiquity, read books and grasped great principles, delighted in composing poetry, was skilled in seal and clerical script, and was especially adept at large characters.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqing loved antiquity, read widely and grasped larger principles, enjoyed poetry, excelled at seal and clerical script, and was especially masterful at large-character writing.

sentences.zh: 世宗行郊禮，受尊號，及受命寶，皆光慶篆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong performed suburban rites, received a honorific title, and received the Mandate Treasure, all were inscribed in seal script by Guangqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong performed the suburban rites, received his honorific title, and received the Mandate Treasure, Guangqing inscribed them all in seal script.

sentences.zh: 凡宮廟榜署經光慶書者，人稱其有法。

translations.literal: Whenever palace and temple plaques and inscriptions passed through Guangqing's brush, people praised their conformity to rule.
translations.idiomatic: Every palace or temple inscription he wrote was praised as true to classical form.

sentences.zh: 典領原廟、坤厚陵、壽安宮工役，不為苛峻，使勞逸相均。

translations.literal: He directed labor at the Original Temple, Kunhou Tomb, and Shou'an Palace, was not harsh or severe, and made toil and rest balance one another.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw construction at the Original Temple, Kunhou Tomb, and Shou'an Palace without harsh demands, balancing labor and rest fairly.

sentences.zh: 身兼數職，勤慎周密，未嘗自伐，世宗獨察之。

translations.literal: He personally held several offices, was diligent, cautious, and thorough, never boasted of himself, and Emperor Shizong alone observed this.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held several offices at once, he was diligent, careful, and thorough and never boasted. Emperor Shizong alone took full notice.

sentences.zh: 初，御史大夫璋請制大金受命寶，有司以秦璽文進，上命以「大金受命萬世之寶」為文。

translations.literal: Earlier, censor-in-chief Zhang requested the making of the Great Jin Mandate Treasure; the offices presented the text of the Qin seal; the emperor ordered the inscription "Great Jin Mandate Treasure for Ten Thousand Generations."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Censor-in-chief Zhang proposed casting the Great Jin Mandate Treasure. The offices submitted the text of the Qin imperial seal, and the emperor ordered the inscription "Great Jin Mandate Treasure for Ten Thousand Generations."

sentences.zh: 徑四寸八分，厚一寸四分，蟠龍紐，高厚各四寸六分有半。

translations.literal: Its diameter was four inches eight tenths, thickness one inch four tenths, with a coiled-dragon knob; height and thickness were each four inches six tenths and a half.
translations.idiomatic: It measured four inches and eight tenths in diameter, one inch and four tenths thick, with a coiled-dragon knob; height and thickness were each four and a half inches.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書張景仁、少府監張僅言典領工事，詔光慶篆之。

translations.literal: Minister of rites Zhang Jingren and director of the Palace Storehouse Zhang Jinyan directed the work; an edict ordered Guangqing to inscribe it in seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of rites Zhang Jingren and director of the Palace Storehouse Zhang Jinyan oversaw the work, and an edict ordered Guangqing to inscribe it.

sentences.zh: 遷同知宣徽院事，改少府監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Privy Portal Office and changed to director of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Privy Portal Office and then director of the Palace Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複右宣徽使。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother; when recalled he served as right privy portal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was recalled as right privy portal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸上京，光慶往上京治儀仗制度，時人以為得宜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong visited the Superior Capital, Guangqing went to the Superior Capital to arrange ritual regalia and regulations; people of the time thought this fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong visited the Superior Capital, Guangqing went ahead to organize ritual regalia and regulations, which contemporaries judged exactly right.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of the reign he died at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 上遣使至祭，賻銀三百兩、重彩十端、絹百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to perform sacrifice, with funeral gifts of three hundred taels of silver, ten bolts of heavy brocade, and a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to offer sacrifice and funeral gifts of three hundred taels of silver, ten bolts of heavy brocade, and a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 平時喜為善言，蓄善藥，號「善善道人」。

translations.literal: In ordinary times he delighted in kind words, stored good medicines, and styled himself "Daoist Master of Kindness upon Kindness."
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary life he loved kind speech, kept medicinal remedies on hand, and called himself the Daoist Master of Doubled Kindness.

sentences.zh: 晚信浮屠法，自作真贊，語皆任達雲。

translations.literal: In his later years he believed in Buddhist law, composed his own true encomium, and the words were all free and cloudlike.
translations.idiomatic: In later life he turned to Buddhism, wrote his own epitaph, and its language was altogether free and unburdened.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：左企弓、虞仲文、曹勇義、康公弼四子者，皆有才識之士，其事遼主數有論建。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The four men Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, and Kang Gongbi were all men of talent and insight; in serving the Liao ruler they repeatedly offered counsel and proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, and Kang Gongbi were all men of talent and judgment who, in serving the Liao emperor, offered counsel again and again.

sentences.zh: 及其受爵僭位，委質二君，隕身逆黨，三者胥失之，哀哉。

translations.literal: Yet when they received enfeoffment and usurped rank, submitted to two rulers, and perished with the rebel party, all three were lost—how lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when they accepted enfeoffment in a usurping regime, submitted themselves to two masters, and died with the rebel faction, they lost honor, loyalty, and life alike. How lamentable.
